explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/790: 'Is it true that l(n) < n^{1−c} for some c > 0?' (Erdős [Er65, p. 188]: 'very likely g(n) < n^{1−c_9} for some c_9 > 0'; [Er73, p. 130]: 'Probably l(n) < n^{1−c} holds for some c > 0'). Lean: ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ n, (l n : ℝ) < n ^ (1 − c), with a real exponent. The reading 'for all sufficiently large n' is necessary (l(1) = 1 = 1^{1−c}) and is stated in the docstring. l, Guarantees and DistinctSubsetSumFree are the definitions checked for erdos_790.parts.i. @[question] fits. Note on status: the page carries an unreviewed proof claim (S. Korsky, submitted 2026-09-13) of l(n) ≫ n/(log n)^2, which would answer this question in the negative. The external problem database still lists 790 as open, so the category agrees with the source today; if the claim is accepted the statement should be negated and retagged. Correct.
